items.title: Seoul, South Korea, South Korea: Foreign investors bought a record $5.4 billion of South Korean stocks on July 31, while domestic retail investors sold a record $5.5 billion, reversing months of heavy foreign selling; brokerage deposits for stock purchases have dropped $23 billion from their June peak.
items.description: Foreign investors bought a record $5.4 billion of South Korean stocks on July 31, while domestic retail investors sold a record $5.5 billion, reversing months of heavy foreign selling; brokerage deposits for stock purchases have dropped $23 billion from their June peak.
items.rawSummary: South Korea's equity market has undergone extreme volatility—a historic crash that wiped out $2 trillion in market cap, a government intervention, and then a sharp rebound on July 31 fueled by record foreign buying—while the defense sector notches milestones with the KF-21 fighter and KSAM-II missile.
items.analysis: South Korea's equity market experienced a historic cycle: a 135% surge between December and June, propelled by chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung, gave way to a 44% decline over 40 days, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market capitalization. The selloff, amplified by record retail leverage in leveraged ETFs and options, triggered a wave of margin calls—Goldman Sachs reported that more than 1.2 million leveraged retail accounts faced margin calls by mid-July, with over 500,000 likely fully liquidated—and assets under management in leveraged ETFs fell 70% from their peak, while margin debt has now declined $4 billion from its June peak to $22 billion, the lowest since mid-April, and leveraged ETF assets tied to the two chip giants collapsed 63% to $4 billion. The finance ministry responded with an emergency meeting, around-the-clock market monitoring, and restrictions on leveraged ETF trading, and after a brief rebound the KOSPI surged nearly 15% in a single day amid a global chip stock rally; data now shows that foreign investors drove the move with a record $5.4 billion in purchases, while domestic retail investors sold a record $5.5 billion, and brokerage deposits for stock buying have fallen sharply from their June peak, signaling an unwinding of the retail leverage cycle. In separate developments, former President Yoon Seok-yeol was sentenced to 18 months for false campaign statements, while the defense sector advanced with the completion of KF-21 Boramae fighter system development and the start of prototype assembly of the indigenous KSAM-II naval surface-to-air missile.

items.title: Beijing, China, China: Reuters reported that China is signaling it will maintain its state-led, export-driven economic model and is entering upcoming trade talks from a confident position, rejecting accusations of overcapacity and unfair subsidies.
items.description: Reuters reported that China is signaling it will maintain its state-led, export-driven economic model and is entering upcoming trade talks from a confident position, rejecting accusations of overcapacity and unfair subsidies.
items.rawSummary: China's economy contracted across manufacturing and services in July while Beijing denied missile transfer reports and Reuters revealed military-linked distillation of U.S. AI models; amid these strains, China signaled it would maintain its state-led export model in upcoming trade talks.
items.analysis: China's economic momentum weakened markedly in July, with the manufacturing PMI falling to 49.2—its first contraction reading since February—and the non-manufacturing PMI dropping to 49.0, the lowest since December 2022, driven by a steep decline in construction activity; GDP growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, the weakest pace since late 2022. The downturn comes as the Foreign Ministry dismissed as false reports that Iran would receive Chinese shoulder-fired air defense missile launchers, reiterating Beijing's commitment to peace. Separately, Reuters revealed that Chinese military-affiliated entities are using model distillation to train domestic AI systems on outputs from OpenAI and Anthropic: North University of China employed Claude to generate synthetic data for social media monitoring, while PLA Unit 96941 used GPT-3.5 to summarize sensitive military source code for a domestically hosted model, highlighting persistent efforts to repurpose U.S. AI capabilities despite chip and model access constraints. Against this backdrop, China is signaling it will not fundamentally change its state-led, export-driven economic model despite pressure from the U.S. and EU, and is approaching upcoming trade talks from a confident position while rejecting accusations of overcapacity and unfair subsidies.

items.title: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, United States: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said the Department of War was ready to go and remains at readiness levels not seen since World War II, though Walter Reed has reported no surge.
items.description: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said the Department of War was ready to go and remains at readiness levels not seen since World War II, though Walter Reed has reported no surge.
items.rawSummary: Diplomatic efforts to avert a U.S. strike on Iran have advanced, with President Trump calling off a planned attack and signaling imminent negotiations, while Walter Reed National Military Medical Center continues normal operations without a surge.
items.analysis: President Trump called off a military strike on Iran after appeals from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and Iran itself, describing the halted operation as the largest since World War II and citing concerns about mass displacement in neighboring countries and a preference to avoid killing people. The Wall Street Journal reported that Qatar presented a new proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Iran signaled openness to negotiations, though disputes persist over shipping lane control and transit fees. Trump said direct talks would begin the next afternoon, emphasizing that a deal on the strait is imminent and would be followed by a nuclear agreement. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth stated the Department of War remains at readiness levels not seen since World War II, but Walter Reed, as the military's premier medical center, has reported no surge and continues to operate at normal readiness, reflecting the diplomatic trajectory.

items.analysis: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez that the EU would continue supporting Spain in tackling illegal migration, and proposed enhancing early-warning border systems while increasing technical and financial support to Morocco. Amid reports of a potential Strait of Hormuz deal, Baghaei clarified that Iran is considering only a limited shipping lane proposal with designated entry and exit points negotiated through Oman, not a full reopening, and that no direct U.S. negotiations are taking place, with Pakistan serving as the primary intermediary and Qatar assisting message exchanges; he said the current restrictions will remain as long as what Iran describes as U.S. military aggression continues. This follows the execution of two men for allegedly providing Mossad with military site coordinates, the Foreign Ministry's assertion that there are no plans for a U.S. delegation exchange, and President Pezeshkian's statement that a newly signed memorandum will become the center of gravity for Iran's foreign relations and regional security, underscoring efforts to consolidate alliances amid the crisis.
